description: Four-tap fixed-kernel decimator on Q12 signed samples: x0=a[11:0], x1=a[23:12], x2=b[11:0], x3=b[23:12] (bits 31:24 don't care) against the binomial taps 512/1536/1536/512 (Q12, unity gain at shift 12), so sum=x0*512+x1*1536+x2*1536+x3*512. sum is rounded half-up, shifted right by c[3:0] and cropped to signed 16-bit into result[15:0] (result[31:16]=0). aux[26:0]=sum, aux[27]=1 when the crop fired, aux[31:28]=the shift actually applied. fault=1 when the crop fired. Response latency is 4 enabled beats and the pipeline accepts one beat per enabled cycle while the tail is ready.
hardware_advantage: Four hard slices plus a registered adder tree retire a 4-tap kernel every enabled beat; a soft processor would need four multiply instructions and three adds in one instruction slot.
provenance: original source authored in this workspace; no third-party RTL imported
qualification: engineering candidate; not certified production or side-channel protection
